how: Playwright driving the locally installed Google Chrome 150 with a CDP virtual authenticator (ctap2_1, internal transport, resident key, UV on)

derived.via: HKDF-SHA256, salt pinesign/v1, info x25519 / secp256k1

gotchas: Playwright 1.56 refuses to download its bundled chromium on macOS 12 ('Playwright does not support chromium on mac12'). Launching with channel: 'chrome' against the installed Google Chrome works and needs no download.

@noble/curves 2.x verify() HASHES the message itself, so a WebAuthn assertion must be verified against the raw authenticatorData || sha256(clientDataJSON), not against its SHA-256. Passing the digest fails silently as a bad signature. The workshop's copy of @noble/curves is 1.x and takes the digest instead, so the two spikes are not interchangeable.

Assertion signatures come back high-s about half the time (observed both ways across runs) and nothing in WebAuthn normalises s. noble's verify defaults to lowS: true and rejects those, so a verifier must pass lowS: false. The EIP-7951 precompile accepts both, which is why the on-chain side is unaffected.
CAVEAT: A virtual authenticator proves the API shape and that PRF output is stable across assertions on one authenticator. It cannot prove that real hardware gives the same PRF bytes on a second physical device: that stays a manual two-device tap, which is docs/TESTING.md section 3 in PineSign and the one check that could still invalidate the design.
